question.text: Ramesh invested Rs. 5,00,000 in a fixed deposit offering 8% annual return. If inflation during the same period was 6%, what is the approximate real rate of return on his investment?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes the real rate of return as the nominal return adjusted for inflation. Using the approximation that the real return equals the nominal return less the inflation rate: 8% - 6% = 2%, which matches option A. The Trap: Option B (8%) is the nominal return without any adjustment for inflation, which is the very thing the real return concept corrects for. Option C (14%) incorrectly adds the nominal return and inflation rate instead of taking the difference. Option D (6%) simply restates the inflation rate rather than the real return. Note: The workbook contrasts nominal return (the headline return) with real return (return adjusted for inflation) so investors can see how much of their nominal gain represents an actual increase in purchasing power.
